questions.stem: How do sunken stomata help xerophytes reduce water loss?

options.text: They prevent sunlight from reaching the stomata
They allow more carbon dioxide to enter the leaf
They create a pocket of humid air that reduces the diffusion gradient for water vapour
They block wind from entering the leaf interior

questions.explanation: Sunken stomata sit in pits below the leaf surface. Water vapour collects in these pits, creating a pocket of humid air. This reduces the water potential gradient between the inside of the leaf and the outside air, slowing down the rate of water loss by transpiration.
